nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-01.title: Fibonacci pattern
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-01.body:
The successive values $\frac11,\frac12,\frac23,\frac35,\frac58$ are ratios of consecutive Fibonacci numbers, since $\frac{1}{1+F_{n-1}/F_n}=\frac{F_n}{F_{n+1}}$. Starting from $\frac11$ and applying this four times gives $\frac58$.

**Answer: $\frac58$**

nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-02.title: Two equations
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-02.body:
With $M$ men and $W$ women: $M+24=2W$ and $M=2(W-x)$. Subtracting, $24=2x$, so $x=12$.

**Answer: 12**

nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-03.title: Fraction of the circumference
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-03.body:
A $40^\circ$ arc is $\frac{40}{360}=\frac19$ of the circle, so $\frac19\cdot2\pi r=3\pi$, giving $r=\frac{27}{2}$.

**Answer: $\frac{27}{2}$**

nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-06.title: Law of cosines
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-06.body:
The largest angle $C$ is opposite the side $7$: $49=9+25-30\cos C$, so $\cos C=-\frac12$ and $C=120^\circ$.

**Answer: $120^\circ$**

nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-07.title: Ratio of sides
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-07.body:
The sides of the squares are in ratio $AC:AB=\sqrt2:1$, so the areas are in ratio $2:1$. The area of $ABCD$ is $\frac82=4$.

**Answer: 4**

nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-08.title: Hypotenuse is a diameter
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-08.body:
The hypotenuse is $\sqrt{\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta}=1$. The hypotenuse of a right triangle is a diameter of its circumcircle, so the radius is $\frac12$.

**Answer: $\frac12$**

nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-09.title: Run time backwards
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-09.body:
The trains approach each other at $70+40=110$ miles per hour. One hour before they meet they are $110$ miles apart. (The distance between the cities is not needed.)

**Answer: 110 miles**

nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-11.title: The coloring repeats
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-11.body:
Cards $1$ and $2$ get different colors: $3\cdot2=6$ ways. Card $3$ must differ from both cards $1$ and $2$, so its color is forced; likewise every later card $n$ must differ from $n-1$ and $n-2$, so it is forced (it gets the color of card $n-3$). Every such coloring works, since cards differing by $1$ or $2$ then always have different colors. So there are $6$ ways.

**Answer: 6**

nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-12.title: Perpendicular bisector of the diagonal
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-12.body:
The crease is the part of the perpendicular bisector of diagonal $AC$ (length $26$) inside the rectangle. It passes through the center $O$, and a half-crease $OX$ ($X$ on a long side) forms a right triangle with half the diagonal similar to the triangle formed by the diagonal and the sides: $\frac{OX}{13}=\frac{10}{24}$. So $OX=\frac{65}{12}$ and the crease is $\frac{65}{6}$.

**Answer: $\frac{65}{6}$**

nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-12.title: Coordinates
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-12.body:
Rectangle $[0,24]\times[0,10]$ with opposite vertices $(0,0)$ and $(24,10)$. Points equidistant from them satisfy $x^2+y^2=(x-24)^2+(y-10)^2$, i.e. $48x+20y=676$. At $y=0$: $x=\frac{169}{12}$; at $y=10$: $x=\frac{119}{12}$. The crease length is $\sqrt{\left(\frac{50}{12}\right)^2+10^2}=\sqrt{\frac{625}{36}+100}=\frac{65}{6}$.

**Answer: $\frac{65}{6}$**

nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-13.title: Divisibility by 11
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-13.body:
The number is $\overline{aabb}=1100a+11b=11(100a+b)$. Being a square divisible by $11$, it is divisible by $121$, so $11\mid 100a+b$, i.e. $11\mid a+b$ (as $100\equiv1$). With digits, $a+b=11$, and the number is $121(9a+1)$, so $9a+1$ must be a square: $a=7$ gives $64$. The number is $121\cdot64=7744=88^2$.

**Answer: 7744**

nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-14.title: Count ordered pairs
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-14.body:
With $n$ seniors, each gives $n-1$ snapshots, so $n(n-1)=870=30\cdot29$, giving $n=30$.

**Answer: 30**

nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-15.title: List outcomes
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-15.body:
The ordered pairs with product $12$ are $(2,6),(6,2),(3,4),(4,3)$: $4$ of the $36$ outcomes, so the probability is $\frac{4}{36}=\frac19$.

**Answer: $\frac19$**

nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-16.title: Cosine of a sum
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-16.body:
Let $A=\operatorname{Arcsin}\frac45$ and $B=\operatorname{Arctan}\frac5{12}$, both in the first quadrant. Then $\cos A=\frac35$, $\sin B=\frac5{13}$, $\cos B=\frac{12}{13}$, and $\cos(A+B)=\frac35\cdot\frac{12}{13}-\frac45\cdot\frac5{13}=\frac{36-20}{65}=\frac{16}{65}$.

**Answer: $\frac{16}{65}$**

nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-16.title: Complex numbers
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-16.body:
$A$ is the argument of $3+4i$ and $B$ the argument of $12+5i$. Their product is $(3+4i)(12+5i)=16+63i$, of modulus $65$, so $\cos(A+B)=\frac{16}{65}$.

**Answer: $\frac{16}{65}$**

nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-17.title: Middle term
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-17.body:
The angles sum to $3\cdot180^\circ=540^\circ$, so their average, the middle term of the progression, is $108^\circ$. The smallest is $108^\circ-20^\circ=88^\circ$.

**Answer: $88^\circ$**

nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-20.title: Factor
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-20.body:
$(b-a)(b+a)=24$, where $b-a$ and $b+a$ have the same parity, so both are even: $(2,12)$ or $(4,6)$. These give $a+b=12$ (with $a=5$, $b=7$) or $a+b=6$ (with $a=1$, $b=5$). The largest is $12$.

**Answer: 12**

nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-21.title: Similar triangles
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-21.body:
Since $DQ\parallel AB$, triangles $QDP$ and $ABP$ are similar with ratio $DP:BP=1:2$. Hence $DQ=\frac12AB=5$.

**Answer: 5**

nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-22.title: Complement
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-22.body:
A product of two dice is prime only if one die shows $1$ and the other a prime $2$, $3$ or $5$: $2\cdot3=6$ outcomes. So the probability of not prime is $1-\frac6{36}=\frac56$.

**Answer: $\frac56$**

nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-24.title: Sum of cubes
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-24.body:
$\sin^6x+\cos^6x=(\sin^2x+\cos^2x)^3-3\sin^2x\cos^2x(\sin^2x+\cos^2x)=1-3\sin^2x\cos^2x=1-\frac34\sin^22x$. Setting this to $\frac23$ gives $\sin^22x=\frac49$. Since $0\le2x\le\pi$, $\sin2x\ge0$, so $\sin2x=\frac23$.

**Answer: $\frac23$**

nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-25.title: Weighted average
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-25.body:
$\frac34$ of the class studied $3$ hours and $\frac14$ studied $2$: $\frac34\cdot3+\frac14\cdot2=\frac{11}{4}$.

**Answer: $2.75$ hours**

nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-26.title: Right trapezoid
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-26.body:
Join the centers $O_1,O_2$ and the points of tangency. Dropping a perpendicular from the smaller center to the larger radius gives a right triangle with hypotenuse $7$, one leg $6$ (the tangent length), and the other leg $R-r$. So $(R-r)^2=49-36=13$ and $R-r=\sqrt{13}$.

**Answer: $\sqrt{13}$**

nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-28.title: Two isosceles triangles
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-28.body:
Let $\angle PQR=x$; then $\angle PSR=x$ and $\angle QPS=180^\circ-x$. Since $PQ=PA$, triangle $PQA$ is isosceles with $\angle PAQ=x$ and $\angle QPA=180^\circ-2x$. Also $PS=PQ=PA=PB$, so triangle $PSB$ is isosceles with $\angle SPB=180^\circ-2x$. The angle at $P$ splits as $\angle QPA+\angle APB+\angle BPS$: $180-x=(180-2x)+60+(180-2x)$, so $3x=240$ and $x=80$.

**Answer: $80^\circ$**

nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-29.title: Pythagoras twice
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-29.body:
A face diagonal is $\sqrt{4^2+4^2}=4\sqrt2$; the space diagonal is $\sqrt{(4\sqrt2)^2+4^2}=\sqrt{48}=4\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $4\sqrt3$**

nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-29.title: Formula
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-29.body:
The space diagonal of a cube of side $s$ is $s\sqrt3$, here $4\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $4\sqrt3$**

nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-30.title: Compare bounds
nyciml-1985-86-spring-seniorb-30.body:
Complete squares: $3x^2+6x+7=3(x+1)^2+4\ge4$ and $5x^2+10x+14=5(x+1)^2+9\ge9$, so the left side is at least $2+3=5$. The right side is $5-(x+1)^2\le5$. Equality requires both to equal $5$, which happens only when $(x+1)^2=0$, i.e. $x=-1$.

**Answer: $-1$**
